questions.question: A sport store offers 19% discount on its articles and it offers a further discount of 2% on the reduced price to those customers who pay by online wallet. If a customer purchase sports items worth ₹ 18000 and pays through an online wallet then the amount (in ₹) to be paid by the customer is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Store offers 19% discount on its articles. 

For payment using an online wallet, a further discount of 2% on the reduced price.

A customer purchases items worth ₹ 18000 using payment through an online wallet.

Concept used:

Discount% = {(Marked Price - Selling Price) over Marked Price} times 100\%

SP = MP - MP × Discount%

Calculation:

Final discount for a customer who pays by Online wallet 

⇒ 19 + 2 - (19 × 2)/100 = 20.62%

Now, the amount paid by the customer

⇒ 18000 - 18000 × 20.62%

⇒ ₹14288.40

**∴ The amount to be paid by the customer is ₹14288.40.**

questions.question: A dealer sells an article by allowing a 13% discount on its marked price and gains 20%. If the cost price of the article is increased by 10%, what discount percentage should he allow now on the same marked price, so as to earn the same percentage of profit as before?
questions.solution:
Given:

A dealer sells an article by allowing a 13% discount on its marked price and gains 20%.

The cost price of the article is increased by 10%.

Concept used:

Selling price = Marked Price - Marked Price × Discount%

Selling Price = Cost Price × (1 + Gain%)

Calculation:

Let the cost price be Q.

Selling price = Q + Q × 20% = 1.2Q

Marked price = 1.2Q ÷ (1 - 13%)

⇒ 1.2Q ÷ 0.87

⇒ 1.379Q ≈ 1.38Q

New cost price = Q + Q × 10% = 1.1Q

New selling price = 1.1Q + 1.1Q × 20%

⇒ 1.32Q

Now, discount% offered = {{1.38Q - 1.32Q} over 1.38Q} times 100\%

⇒ 4.34% ≈ 4.3%

∴ He should allow a 4.3% discount on the marked price.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**Let the MP be 100

SP = 100 - (100 × 13%)

SP = 87

CP = 87/1.20 = 72.5

New CP = 72.5 + (72.5 × 10%) = 79.75

New SP = 79.75 + (79.75 × 20%) = 95.7

∴ The max discount that can be offered is 100 - 95.7 = 4.3%

questions.question: The cost prices of two articles are in the ratio 4 : 5. Selling the first article at 10% profit and the second at 20% profit will give the difference of ₹480 in their selling prices. The sum of the cost price of the two article is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The cost prices of the two articles are in the ratio 4 : 5.

Selling the first article at 10% profit and the second at 20% profit 

The difference of Rs 480 in their selling prices.

**Concept used:**

Selling Price = CP + (Profit percentage / 100) × CP

**Calculation:**

Let, the cost price be 4x and 5x

The selling price of the 1st article is

4x + 4x × (10/100)

⇒ 4x + 0.4x

⇒ 4.4x

The selling price of the 2nd article is

5x + 5x × (20/100)

⇒ 5x + x

⇒ 6x

As per the question,

6x - 4.4x = 480

⇒ 1.6x = 480

⇒ x = 480 / 1.6

⇒ x = 300

So the total cost price of two article = 4x + 5x = 9x

Value of 9x = 9 × 300 = Rs 2700

**∴ The cost price is Rs 2700**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__** Among the given options, 2700 is only divisible by 9.

And from the question, it is clear that the option will be a multiple of 9 = (4 + 5) always

So, the answer will be Rs 2700

questions.question: A merchant purchased 650 kg of wheat at Rs. 50 per kg. He sold 250 kg of it at a profit of 24% and 200 kg at a loss of 24%. At what rate per kg (in Rs.) should he sell the remaining wheat to gain 20% on his initial investment?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

According to the question-

Selling price of 250 kg of wheat = 1.24 × Rs 50 = Rs 62

Selling price of 200 kg of wheat = 0.76 × Rs 50 = Rs 38

Remaining wheat = 650 - (200 + 250) = 200 kg

Expected gain = 1.2 × Rs 50 = Rs 60.

Let the selling price of remaining wheat be "a"

⇒ 650 × 60 = (250 × 62) + (200 × 38) + (200 × a)

⇒ 200a = 39000 - (15500 + 7600)

⇒ a = 15,900 ÷ 200 = 79.5

∴ **The cost of remaining wheat should be Rs 79.5 per kg.**

questions.question: Raju buys 75 articles at the same price each. He sells one-third of them at a profit of 40% and 20% of the remaining at a profit of 20%. He sells the remaining articles at a loss equal to the cost price of 7 articles. What is his gain/loss per cent in the entire transaction?
questions.solution:
Given:

Raju buys 75 articles at the same price each. He sells one-third of them at a profit of 40% and 20% of the remaining at a profit of 20%. 

He sells the remaining articles at a loss equal to the cost price of 7 articles. 

Concept used:

profit% = {(Selling Price - Cost Price) over Cost Price} times 100\%

Selling Price = Cost Price + Cost Price × Gain%

Calculation

Let the cost price of each article be Rs. 1.

The cost price of 7 articles = Rs. 7

The cost price of 75 articles = Rs. 75

The cost price of 25 articles i.e. (1/3)rd of 75 = Rs. 25

The selling price of 25 articles = 25 + 40% of 25

⇒ 25 + 10 = Rs. 35

Number of remaining articles after selling 25 articles = 75 - 25 = 50

The cost price of 10 articles i.e. 20% of 50 = Rs. 10

The selling price of 10 articles at 20% profit = 10 + 20% of 10

⇒10 + 2 = Rs. 12

Number of articles left after selling 35 articles = 50 - 10 = 40

The cost price of 40 articles = Rs. 40

The selling price of 40 articles

⇒ The cost price of 40 articles - the cost price of 7 articles

⇒ 40 - 7 = Rs. 33

Total selling price = 35 + 12 + 33 = Rs. 80

The total cost price = Rs. 75

Now, profit % = {(80 - 75) over 75} times 100\%

⇒ (5/75) × 100%

⇒ 100/15 %

⇒ 20/3 %

⇒ 62over3%

**∴ His gain percentage in the entire transaction is 62over3%.**

questions.question: The selling price of an article is Rs. 624 when it is sold at 30% profit. If the cost price of the article is increased by Rs. 50 and the selling price is increased by Rs. 60, then what will be the profit percentage (nearest to an integer)?
questions.solution:
Given:

Selling Price = Rs. 624

Profit = 30%

The cost price of the article is increased by Rs. 50 and the selling price is increased by Rs. 60.

Concept used:

Selling Price = Cost Price × (1 + Gain%)

Profit% = {(Selling Price - Cost Price) over Cost Price} times 100\%

Calculation:

Let the cost price of the article be Rs. Q.

According to the concept,

Q + Q × 30% = 624

⇒ Q + 0.3Q = 624

⇒ 1.3Q = 624

⇒ Q = 624/1.3

⇒ Q = 480

Increased cost price = (480 + 50) = Rs. 530

Increased selling price = (624 + 60) = Rs. 684

Now, profit% = {{684 - 530} over 530} times 100\%

⇒ {{154} over 530} times 100\% 

⇒ 29.05% ≈ 29%

∴ The profit percentage is 29%.
